A common response when people complain about censorship on say, Reddit, seems to be that since it isn't the government doing it, it's not really censorship and private websites are free to do as they please. While it is true a private website can delete whatever it wants, it is NOT true that it doesn't count as censorship.

From ACLU's "What is Censorship" page:

Censorship, the suppression of words, images, or ideas that are "offensive," happens whenever some people succeed in imposing their personal political or moral values on others. Censorship can be carried out by the government as well as private pressure groups.

I think it is important to bring this up any time someone tries to invoke that defense.
"Censorship can be carried out by the government as well as private pressure groups." -The ACLU

Agreed. The act of censorship need not involve police or soldiers locking the doors to a library, bookstore or art gallery.

When American Express, Mastercard and Visa stop providing financial services to Backpage.com, that's a subtle form of censorship. When Paypal refuses to process payments to Protonmail.ch, Wikileaks, SeekingArrangement.com, etc. that's a subtle form of censorship.

Paypal's refusal to process donations to Voat is also a form of censorship.

New times, new modalities of censorship.
